paragraphs.en: Tip woke up shortly after dawn, while the Scarecrow had already gathered some ripe berries from nearby bushes. The boy ate them eagerly and then they continued their journey.
paragraphs.zh: 提普在黎明不久后醒来，而稻草人已经从附近的灌木丛中摘了一些成熟的浆果。男孩迫不及待地吃了下去，然后他们继续前行。

paragraphs.en: An hour later, they reached the top of a hill where they could see the City of the Winkies and the tall domes of the Emperor's palace among simpler houses.
paragraphs.zh: 一个多小时后，他们来到了一个山顶，从这里可以眺望到 winkies 城市以及皇帝宫殿高高的圆顶，在它们周围是更为简朴的房屋。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow became excited at this sight. "I am so happy to see my old friend the Tin Woodman again! I hope he has ruled his people better than I did."
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人看到这一幕兴奋不已：“我真是太高兴再次见到我的老朋友铁皮人了！我希望他治理自己的子民比我做得更好。”

paragraphs.en: "Is the Tin Woodman the Emperor?" asked the horse.
paragraphs.zh: “锡人就是皇帝吗？”马问道。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, they invited him after the Wicked Witch was defeated," replied the Scarecrow. "Nick Chopper has the best heart in all the world, so he must be an excellent emperor."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，巫婆被打败后他们邀请了他的。”稻草人回答说，“尼克·钩子拥有一颗世界上最善良的心，所以他一定是位出色的皇帝。”

paragraphs.en: Tip interjected, "I thought 'Emperor' meant someone who rules an empire, not a kingdom."
paragraphs.zh: Tip插嘴道：“我以为‘皇帝’是指统治帝国的人，而不是王国。”

paragraphs.en: "Don't say that to the Tin Woodman!" the Scarecrow warned. "It would hurt his feelings.
paragraphs.zh: “别对锡人说这种话！”稻草人警告道，“他会伤了心的。”

paragraphs.en: He is proud and loves being called Emperor."
paragraphs.zh: 他骄傲无比，尤其喜欢别人称他为皇帝。

paragraphs.en: The horse moved quickly, making it hard for Tip to stay on its back. They didn’t talk much until they reached the palace steps.
paragraphs.zh: 马儿跑得飞快，蒂普好不容易才稳住坐骑。两人一路上很少交谈，直到抵达宫殿的台阶前。

paragraphs.en: An elderly Winkie in a silver uniform approached to help them down. The Scarecrow said, "Take us directly to your master, the Emperor."
paragraphs.zh: 一位身穿银色制服的老年温基人走过来帮助他们下来。稻草人说道：“请直接带我们去见你们的皇帝陛下。”

paragraphs.en: The man hesitated and replied, "I'm afraid you must wait. The Emperor is not receiving visitors today."
paragraphs.zh: 那人犹豫了一下，回答说：“恐怕您得等等了。皇帝今天不接见客人。”

paragraphs.en: "Why not?" asked the Scarecrow anxiously.
paragraphs.zh: “为什么不行？”稻草人焦虑地问道。

paragraphs.en: "He's being polished," explained the man. "His august presence is covered in putz-pomade right now."
paragraphs.zh: 他正在被打磨，那人解释道：“他的尊贵身姿此刻正被一层凡油膏覆盖着。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I see!" said the Scarecrow, relieved. "My friend was always a dandy and probably more proud of his appearance than ever."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我明白了！”稻草人松了口气，“我的朋友一向风度翩翩，恐怕对自己的外表更加得意了。”

paragraphs.en: The man bowed politely and added, "Our mighty Emperor has recently been nickel-plated."
paragraphs.zh: 那人礼貌地鞠了一躬，又补充道：“我们的皇帝陛下最近可说是镀了层镍。”

paragraphs.en: "Good Gracious!" exclaimed the Scarecrow upon hearing this. "If his wit is as polished, it must be sparkling!
paragraphs.zh: “天哪！”稻草人惊叫道，“如果他的智慧如此锋利，那必定璀璨夺目！”

paragraphs.en: But show us in—I'm sure the Emperor will receive us."
paragraphs.zh: 但是请带我们进去——我相信皇帝会接见我们的。

paragraphs.en: The man replied, "The Emperor's state is always magnificent. I'll venture to tell him of your arrival and await his commands."
paragraphs.zh: 那人回答道：“陛下的风采永远令人赞叹。我这就去禀告陛下您的到来，并恭候他的吩咐。”

paragraphs.en: They entered a splendid ante-room, with the Saw-Horse awkwardly following behind, unaware that horses were not expected inside.
paragraphs.zh: 他们步入了一个华丽的前厅，那匹锯马则笨拙地跟在后面，全然不知马是不被允许进入这里的。

paragraphs.en: Initially awed by their surroundings, the travelers admired rich silver hangings and a center-table adorned with an oil-can engraved with scenes from past adventures. Portraits hung on the walls; the Scarecrow's seemed most prominent.
paragraphs.zh: 初来乍到时，旅人们被周围的景象所震撼，赞叹那些华丽的银质窗帘和中央桌上摆放的一盏雕刻着往昔冒险场景的油灯。墙上挂着肖像画，稻草人先生的画像显得尤为显眼。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, they heard a loud voice in the next room: "Well! What a great surprise!" The door burst open, revealing Nick Chopper rushing to embrace the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，他们听到隔壁房间里传来一个响亮的声音：“嘿！真是个意外的惊喜！”门猛然被推开，只见尼克·切普勒急匆匆地冲过来拥抱稻草人。

paragraphs.en: "My dear old friend! My noble comrade!" cried the Tin Woodman joyfully.
paragraphs.zh: “我亲爱的老朋友！我的高贵同伴！”铁皮人高兴地喊道。

paragraphs.en: "How delighted I am to meet you again."
paragraphs.zh: “再次见到你，我真是太高兴了。”

paragraphs.en: He released the Scarecrow and examined his beloved features closely. However, the Scarecrow's face and body bore blotches of putz-pomade; in his eagerness, Nick Chopper had rubbed paste from himself onto his friend.
paragraphs.zh: 他释放了稻草人，仔细端详起他心爱的面容。然而，稻草人的脸上和身上沾满了发蜡的斑点；在匆忙之中，Nick Chopper 不自觉地把自己身上的发蜡抹到了朋友身上。

paragraphs.en: "Dear me!" said the Scarecrow dolefully. "What a mess!"
paragraphs.zh: “唉！”稻草人沮丧地说，“真是乱七八糟！”

paragraphs.en: "Don't worry," replied the Tin Woodman. "I'll send you to my Imperial Laundry and you'll come out as good as new."
paragraphs.zh: “别担心，”锡头人说道，“我会把你送到我的御用洗衣坊，洗完后你就像新的一样。”

paragraphs.en: "No mangled?" asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.zh: “没有残缺吗？”稻草人问道。

paragraphs.en: "Not at all!" was the reply. "Now, how did your Majesty arrive here?
paragraphs.zh: “根本不是那么回事！”皇帝回答道，“那您是怎么来到这里的呢，陛下？”

paragraphs.en: And who are your companions?"
paragraphs.zh: “你的同伴是谁？”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow introduced Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead, whose presence greatly interested the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人介绍了Tip和南瓜头Jack，他们的出现让铁皮木人感到非常好奇。

paragraphs.en: The Emperor admitted Jack was not substantial but unusual enough to join their society. Jack humbly thanked him.
paragraphs.zh: 皇帝承认杰克虽然不够实在，但个性独特，足以加入他们的行列。杰克谦逊地向他道谢。

paragraphs.en: "I hope you are in good health?" asked the Woodman.
paragraphs.zh: “希望你身体康健？”伐木工问道。

paragraphs.en: Jack sighed, replying, "Yes, for now, but I fear the day when I might spoil."
paragraphs.zh: 杰克叹了口气，回答说：“是的，目前还行，但我担心有一天我会放纵。”

paragraphs.en: "Nonsense," said the Emperor kindly. "You can be canned before that happens, preserving your head indefinitely."
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道，”皇帝和蔼地说，“你还没到那种地步就会被解雇，你的脑袋可以永远保存下来。”

paragraphs.en: Tip stared at the Woodman in amazement as he noticed the Emperor was made of tin pieces soldered together. The Emperor moved with a slight clanking sound but appeared well-constructed.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普惊讶地盯着木人国王，只见他由锡片焊接而成。皇帝移动时发出轻微的叮当声，但看起来结构还算坚固。

paragraphs.en: The Woodman asked his friends to excuse him while he retired for polishing. In a short time, his nickel-plated body shone magnificently, impressing the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.zh: 木匠请朋友们原谅他一下，自己去打理一番。不一会儿，他的镍镀层身体闪耀着金属的光泽，让稻草人印象深刻。

paragraphs.en: Nick explained that the nickel plating was necessary due to scratches from adventures and noted an engraved star on his chest indicating his heart's location.
paragraphs.zh: 尼克解释说，镍镀层是由于历险中留下的刮痕而必需的，并指出他胸前刻有一颗星星，表明那是他的心脏所在的位置。

paragraphs.en: The Pumpkinhead curiously asked if Nick’s heart was a hand-organ. Nick replied with dignity that it was a large, warm heart, though orthodox.
paragraphs.zh: 南瓜头好奇地问尼克的心是不是一个手风琴。尼克以尊严的语气回答说，他的心很大、很温暖，尽管这与正统观念有所不同。

paragraphs.en: Turning to the Scarecrow, the Emperor inquired about his subjects' happiness. The Scarecrow responded that girls had revolted and driven him from the Emerald City.
paragraphs.zh: 皇帝转向稻草人，询问他的子民是否幸福。稻草人回答说，女孩们发动了叛乱，把他赶出了翡翠城。

paragraphs.en: The Woodman expressed shock at this news, asking if they complained of his rule.
paragraphs.zh: 木匠听到这个消息大吃一惊，问道：“他们抱怨过你的统治吗？”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow explained, "They have taken my city and treasury, and are ruling as they please." The Emperor was shocked and exclaimed, "What an extraordinary idea!"
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人解释说：“他们占领了我的城市和国库，并且随心所欲地统治着。”皇帝听后大吃一惊，脱口而出：“真是个离奇的想法！”

paragraphs.en: Tip added that the females planned to capture the Tin Woodman's castle. The Emperor quickly decided, "We must recapture the Emerald City immediately."
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普补充说，雌性们计划捉住锡头王的城堡。皇帝迅速下了决定：“我们必须立即夺回翡翠城。”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow replied happily, "I knew you would help me. How many soldiers can you gather?"
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人高兴地回答：“我知道你会帮助我的。你能召集多少士兵？”

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman corrected, "With my axe, we four are enough." Jack then said, "Actually, it’s five; the Saw-Horse is brave too."
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人纠正道：“有了我的斧头，我们四个人足够了。”杰克随后说：“其实应该是五个人；木马骑士也很勇敢。”

paragraphs.en: Puzzled, the Tin Woodman noticed the Saw-Horse standing quietly in a corner. Tip called it over, and it awkwardly approached, nearly tipping the center-table.
paragraphs.zh: 困惑间，锡人木偶注意到锯马安静地站在角落里。蒂普把它叫了过来，锯马笨拙地走了过来，差点儿把中央的小茶几撞翻了。

paragraphs.en: The Emperor asked, "How did you bring this creature to life?" Jack modestly replied, "With magic powder, and he’s been very useful."
paragraphs.zh: 皇帝问道：“你是怎么让这生物复活的？”杰克谦虚地回答道：“靠魔法粉末，他非常有用。”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow added, "He helped us escape the rebels." The Emperor declared, "We must accept him. A live Saw-Horse is a novelty."
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人补充道：“他帮我们逃过了叛军的追捕。”皇帝宣布：“我们必须接纳他。活生生的木马可是件新鲜事儿。”

paragraphs.en: The emperor continued, "Does he know anything?" The Saw-Horse responded, "I have little experience but learn quickly, often knowing more than others."
paragraphs.zh: 皇帝接着问：“他懂得什么？”木马回答道：“我经验不多，但学得快，往往比别人知道得多。”

paragraphs.en: The emperor concluded, "Time is precious; let’s prepare to start our journey."
paragraphs.zh: 皇帝说道：“时间宝贵，让我们准备启程吧。”

paragraphs.en: The emperor instructed his Lord High Chancellor on running the kingdom during his absence. Meanwhile, Tip repaired Jack Pumpkinhead's wooden limbs, making them stronger, and ensured the Saw-Horse was in good condition. The Scarecrow, now cleaned and resplendent with a polished crown, strutted proudly.
paragraphs.zh: 皇帝吩咐首席宰相在自己缺席期间管理王国的事务。与此同时，蒂普修复了杰克南瓜头的木制四肢，使其更加坚固，并确保锯齿马处于良好的状态。稻草人现在被清理得干干净净，戴着一顶磨光的王冠，昂首挺胸地走来走去，显得格外自豪。

paragraphs.en: Bright and early the next morning, they embarked on their journey back to the Emerald City. The Tin Woodman led, carrying a gleaming axe, while Jack Pumpkinhead rode the Saw-Horse. Tip and the Scarecrow walked beside him, ensuring safety.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，他们便启程返回翡翠城。铁皮人走在最前面，手持一把闪亮的斧头开路；杰克南瓜头则骑在锯马身上紧跟其后。托普和稻草人紧随其侧，确保安全。

paragraphs.en: General Jinjur, who had commanded the Army of Revolt, was uneasy about the Scarecrow's escape. She feared that joining forces with the emperor and Tin Woodman could be dangerous for her army. Remembering their past adventures, she sent for Mombi, promising rewards if she helped defeat them.
paragraphs.zh: 金jur将军曾指挥过叛军，对于稻草人逃走一事感到不安。她担心与皇帝和锡铁人联手可能会对自己军队构成威胁。想起他们过去共同经历的种种冒险，金jur将军派人召来了蒙比，许诺如果蒙比能帮助击败他们，将会给予丰厚的报酬。

paragraphs.en: Mombi, furious over Tip’s trick and the theft of the Powder of Life, readily agreed to assist Jinjur. Upon arriving at the palace, Mombi used her magic to discover the adventurers' plans. She then locked herself in a tower room to thwart their return.
paragraphs.zh: 莫比因蒂普的恶作剧和生命粉末被盗而怒火中烧，欣然同意帮助金朱儿。抵达宫殿后，莫比施展魔法探知了冒险者的计划。随后，她把自己关在塔楼的一间房间里，以阻止他们返回。

paragraphs.en: That was why the Tin Woodman stopped, preparing for an encounter with Mombi's magical defenses.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是铁皮人停下的原因，他做好了应对莫伯米魔法防御的准备。

paragraphs.en: Something curious has happened, and Dorothy knows they've lost their way despite knowing every step of the journey. The Scarecrow is shocked by this claim.
paragraphs.zh: 一件奇怪的事情发生了，尽管多萝西对这段旅程的每一步都了如指掌，但她确信他们迷路了。稻草人听到这个说法时大吃一惊。

paragraphs.en: "Impossible!" he protests. "Why do you think we're astray?"
paragraphs.zh: “不可能！”他脱口而出，“你认为我们迷路了是什么意思？”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy points out a field of sunflowers that none have seen before. Each stalk bears a gigantic sunflower, and these flowers whirl around like miniature windmills, blinding everyone.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西指出了一个前所未见的向日葵田。每一株茎上都长着巨大的向日葵，这些花朵像微型风车一样旋转，让所有人都感到眼花缭乱。

paragraphs.en: "It's witchcraft!" exclaims Tip.
paragraphs.zh: “这是巫术！”蒂普脱口而出。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman, impatient, swings his axe to cut down the stalks but finds faces appear in the center of each flower. These faces mock them before bursting into laughter.
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人不耐烦地挥舞着斧头砍向那些茎秆，却发现每朵花的中心竟然出现了人脸。这些面孔嘲笑他们一番后，突然爆发出一阵哄笑。

paragraphs.en: "Stop! stop!" cries Tip, grabbing the Woodman’s arm.
paragraphs.zh: “停！停！”提普喊道，一把抓住樵木的手臂。

paragraphs.en: "They're alive! They’re girls!"
paragraphs.zh: “她们还活着！而且是女孩！”

paragraphs.en: The flowers whirl again, and the faces vanish. The Tin Woodman drops his axe, sitting dejectedly on the ground.
paragraphs.zh: 花朵再次旋舞，那些面孔渐渐消失。黄铜心木人放下斧头，沮丧地坐在地上。

paragraphs.en: "It would be heartless to chop down those pretty creatures," he says, "but I don't know how else we can proceed."
paragraphs.zh: “砍掉这些漂亮的家伙未免太无情了，”他说，“但我不知道还能有什么别的办法。”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow muses that these faces resemble the Army of Revolt but wonders how girls could have followed them so quickly. Tip believes it's magic and suggests it might just be an illusion.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人沉思着，这些面孔看起来像起义军，但他疑惑女孩们怎么会跟得这么紧。Tip认为这是魔法，并建议这可能只是一个幻象。

paragraphs.en: "Let us shut our eyes and walk forward," proposes the Woodman.
paragraphs.zh: “让我们闭上眼睛向前走吧，”樵夫提议道。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow replies, "My eyes are not painted to shut. Because you have tin eyelids doesn't mean we all do."
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人回答说：“我的眼睛并不是画出来的，能够闭合。你有锡制的眼睑，并不意味着我们所有人都是。”

paragraphs.en: Jack leans forward to examine the Saw-Horse’s knot eyes, adding a small detail to the scene.
paragraphs.zh: 杰克凑上前仔细端详锯马那双结状的眼睛，为这幕场景添上了细微但重要的细节。

paragraphs.en: Tip ordered the Pumpkinhead to ride forward quickly, while they would follow to escape. With eyes closed, the Pumpkinhead obeyed, guided by the Saw-Horse's stub tail. The Scarecrow and Tin Woodman brought up the rear.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普命令南瓜头迅速向前骑，他们则紧随其后以求脱身。闭着眼睛的南瓜头听从了吩咐，在木马短粗的尾巴引导下前行。稻草人和铁皮人殿后。

paragraphs.en: Jack's joyful shout signaled a clear path ahead.
paragraphs.zh: 杰克欣喜若狂的喊声预示着前方一片坦途。

paragraphs.en: They paused to look back but found no trace of the sunflower field. More cheerfully, they continued their journey. However, Mombi’s magic had altered the landscape, making them rely on the sun for direction.
paragraphs.zh: 他们停了下来，回头望了一眼，却不见向日葵田的踪迹。于是他们更加欢快地继续前行。然而，蒙比施了魔法，改变了这里的地形，让他们只能依靠太阳来辨别方向。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow decided this was safe as witchcraft couldn't change the sun's course.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人决定这没什么危险，因为巫术改变不了太阳的运行轨迹。

paragraphs.en: The Saw-Horse stumbled into a rabbit hole and fell, sending the Pumpkinhead flying. Tip quickly reattached it to the Saw-Horse's neck and placed Jack back on his feet. But the Saw-Horse’s leg was broken and needed repair before they could proceed.
paragraphs.zh: 木马战车绊倒在了一个兔子洞上，摔了个跟头，把南瓜头弹飞了。蒂普迅速将南瓜头重新固定在木马战车的脖子上，并让杰克重新站稳脚跟。但木马战车的一条腿骨折了，需要修理好他们才能继续前行。

paragraphs.en: "The situation is serious," said the Tin Woodman. "I might make another leg if there were trees nearby, but I see nothing around."
paragraphs.zh: “情况危急，”锡头人说道，“如果附近有树木的话，我或许能再做一条腿，但现在看来四周一片空旷。”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow added that neither fences nor houses were in sight. "What should we do?" asked Tip.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人补充说，既看不见篱笆，也看不见房子。“那我们该怎么办呢？”提普问道。

paragraphs.en: "Let's all think," replied the Scarecrow. "We may find a way to fix the Saw-Horse."
paragraphs.zh: “让我们都动动脑筋，”稻草人回答说，“也许我们可以找到办法修理木马锯子。”

paragraphs.en: They sat on the grass and began to ponder while the Saw-Horse examined its broken leg. The Tin Woodman asked if it hurt, but the Saw-Horse replied that it didn't, though its pride was wounded by finding itself so fragile.
paragraphs.zh: 他们坐在草地上，开始思索起来。锯木马正在检查它那断裂的腿。铁皮人问锯木马疼不疼，但锯木马回答说并不疼，尽管它的自尊心因发现自己如此脆弱而受到了伤害。

paragraphs.en: After some silence, the Tin Woodman looked over the fields, hoping for a solution.
paragraphs.zh: 沉默了一会儿后，锡人木匠环顾着田野，希望能找到解决的办法。

paragraphs.en: He asked curiously, "What kind of creature is approaching us?"
paragraphs.zh: 他好奇地问道：“有什么东西正朝我们走来？”

paragraphs.en: They saw an extraordinary object moving quickly towards them. It stood before the adventurers, looking as surprised as they were.
paragraphs.zh: 他们眼前出现了一个令人惊讶的物体，正快速朝他们逼近。这个物体就站在冒险者面前，显得和他们一样惊讶不已。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow remained calm and greeted politely: "Good morning!"
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人保持冷静，礼貌地打招呼：“早上好！”

paragraphs.en: The stranger removed his hat dramatically, bowed deeply, then said:
paragraphs.zh: 陌生人摘下帽子，戏剧性地鞠了一躬，然后说道：

paragraphs.en: "Good morning, everyone. I hope you are all in good health. Allow me to present my card."
paragraphs.zh: 大家早上好。但愿各位身体康健。让我先递上我的名片。

paragraphs.en: He offered a card which the Scarecrow examined before passing it to Tip.
paragraphs.zh: 他递上一张名片，稻草人先看了看才递给Tip。

paragraphs.en: Tip read aloud: "MR. H. M. WOGGLE-BUG, T. E."
paragraphs.zh: 提普朗声念道：“H·M·沃格勒-布格上校”

paragraphs.en: The Pumpkinhead stared intently and said, "How peculiar!"
paragraphs.zh: 南瓜头专注地盯着对方，脱口而出：“真是怪异！”

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman added, "Very strange."
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人补充道：“真是怪事一桩。”

paragraphs.en: Tip's eyes widened in wonder, while the Saw-Horse sighed and turned its head away.
paragraphs.zh: 提普的眼睛惊讶地睁大了，而锯马则叹了口气，把头转开了。

paragraphs.en: "Are you really a Woggle-Bug?" asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.zh: “你真的是沃格比虫吗？”稻草人问道。
